PullRequest.Title: mcp: support remote URL variables
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- Support declared URL variables when installing remote MCP servers
- Preserve fixed variable values, including empty strings, without creating unnecessary prompts.
- Reject conflicting URL/header input definitions instead of discarding defaults, choices, or secret metadata.

Fixes #336624

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

The MCP Registry's `2025-12-11` schema allows remote transports to declare their own URL variables. The existing converter handled variables inside headers and arguments but copied remote URLs unchanged. A manifest such as the [Dynatrace server manifest](https://github.com/Dynatrace/dynatrace-for-ai/blob/main/server.json) therefore left its environment placeholder unresolved in the generated configuration.

### Registry schema references

- The published [`2025-12-11` JSON Schema](https://static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/2025-12-11/server.schema.json) defines this manifest format.
- The source schema defines [`RemoteTransport.variables`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/main/docs/reference/api/openapi.yaml#L900-L912) as configuration variables referenced by `{curly_braces}` in URL templates.
- [`ServerDetail.remotes[]`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/main/docs/reference/api/openapi.yaml#L999-L1002) explicitly references `RemoteTransport`.
- Remote URL variables were introduced in [modelcontextprotocol/registry#570](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/pull/570) and released in the `2025-12-11` schema by [modelcontextprotocol/registry#841](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/pull/841).

This change implements that specific schema feature. It does not claim complete support for every field added after the earlier registry schema shape.

### Implementation

Remote transport types now expose the URL-variable map separately from package transports. Shared normalization replaces each declared placeholder with its explicit fixed value or a VS Code input reference. The same transformation is used for URL, header, environment, and argument conversion, and for registry-only URL matching.

Fixed-value declarations do not generate interactive inputs. Equivalent URL/header input definitions are deduplicated; incompatible definitions throw a localized error that propagates through existing installation error handling. In particular, a non-secret URL definition cannot silently override a secret header input with the same ID.

### Behavior and constraints

- SSE and streamable HTTP share the conversion path and continue using the existing runtime configuration resolver.
- An explicit empty value remains empty, while a default still belongs to a configurable input.
- Replacement processes every occurrence in one pass. Declared names are escaped for literal matching, replacement text is not recursively interpreted, and undeclared placeholders remain unchanged.
- Registry-only access still requires exact equality with the original URL or its converted representation. This does not introduce wildcard URL matching or permit replacing a declared fixed value with a prompt.
- Fixed values are scoped to their originating declaration and do not enter the shared interactive-input namespace.
- Existing runtime resolution, transport selection, and input persistence remain unchanged.

</details>

Scenarios.Scenario: Browse or inspect MCP gallery entries and evaluate install eligibility under enterprise allow/deny policy
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A gallery page network request and deserialization must complete before entries render; policy evaluation then synchronously derives one identity per entry when install actions/status are queried. The new normalization is in-memory and does not add to the network critical path beyond small per-entry string processing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch one paginated MCP gallery result page (default 50 entries).
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for the first page and one request for each explicitly requested next page; each page contains at most the requested page size (default 50).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same gallery page request and deserialization occurred before the diff; the diff only preserves remote variable metadata and normalizes an entry URL in memory when policy is evaluated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The requested page must arrive before its entries can be displayed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of gallery entries whose install state is evaluated, multiplied by the small number of declared variables in the first remote transport. Each helper invocation scans one URL and its declaration keys.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Pagination is demand-driven and sequential by cursor. URL normalization itself is synchronous per evaluated server and does not spawn concurrent work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is introduced or defeated. Gallery paging and existing service behavior are unchanged; normalization is recomputed when policy evaluation is requested but only over per-entry metadata.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that regex construction/allocation is real and diff-introduced, but high confidence that its realistic cardinality and frequency are too small to constitute a concrete regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Registry manifests do not expose explicit local cardinality bounds for variable maps, but realistic MCP URL templates contain only a few variables and URLs are short.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new CPU/allocation cost is bounded per entry, adds no I/O, and is not on a frame/input loop.

Scenarios.Scenario: Install a remote MCP server from the gallery or a local manifest with URL/header variables
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Manifest conversion and policy validation run synchronously before the existing configuration-resource write. The new URL replacement and input conflict checks must finish before persistence, but operate only on one selected remote plus its headers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve or fetch the gallery server manifest before installation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful lookup in the common case; existing fallback endpoints may be tried sequentially if earlier lookups fail.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Gallery lookup already occurred; remote variable fields are now retained but no additional request is made.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Manifest retrieval must complete before conversion and installation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the converted server and input configuration through addMcpServers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped configuration update for the single installation request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same configuration update occurred before the diff; only the URL/header values and input metadata supplied to it change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The write must complete before installation returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Declared URL variables plus header variables for the selected remote. Replacement is proportional to URL/header text and declaration count; deduplication compares URL-derived inputs with header-derived inputs, which are realistically small manifest-local collections.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One manifest conversion runs per install. Existing gallery resolution and file persistence sequencing are unchanged; the diff adds no parallel tasks or limiter bypass.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No changed cache behavior. Conversion is intentionally performed for each explicit installation; no repeated miss or negative-cache loop is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call path and unchanged I/O cardinality. The possible quadratic in-memory deduplication is real only in variable count and is not a realistic performance bug for MCP manifests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Malformed user-selected manifests can contain unusually large maps because this conversion path accepts parsed input, but that is a one-shot user action and there is no evidence of realistic sizes large enough for visible latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added work is small install-time CPU/allocation before an unchanged single persistence operation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Synchronize installed MCP servers with the registry and compute registry-only enablement
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On startup or MCP/profile/gallery changes, installed server metadata is resolved from the gallery; after responses arrive, enablement scanning compares each installed remote URL against its gallery remotes. The changed normalization runs after the network response and before enabled definitions are published.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve gallery metadata for each distinct installed server name, with endpoint fallbacks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical resolution per unique installed server name; resolutions run concurrently, and each may try up to the existing configured lookup endpoints sequentially until success.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-unique-name concurrent gallery resolution occurred before the diff. The diff adds only an in-memory converted-template equality alternative after metadata is available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Registry-only membership cannot be refreshed until the relevant resolutions settle; prior verified state is retained on failures.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read installed MCP configuration resources and, during discovery sync, resolve one text model per distinct MCP resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Configuration reads follow existing profile/workspace resources; discovery coalesces text-model work by distinct resource, not by server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same configuration scanning and per-resource model lookup happened before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Installed definitions require these reads; URL-template normalization does not alter their count or placement.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed MCP server count after name deduplication; each remote server checks its gallery remote list and only constructs a replacement regex when raw equality fails. Realistic lists contain one or very few remotes and variables.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Registry resolutions use the pre-existing Promise.all across deduplicated server names, while each server's fallback URLs are sequential. Change events are coalesced through the existing throttler/delayer. The normalization adds no concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Gallery identity is associated with the current registry generation and invalidated only on manifest/profile/install changes. No cache key, positive/negative cache state, or invalidation rule is changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the changed branch is reached only for registry-only remote enablement and that all expensive boundary fan-out is pre-existing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users may install many MCP servers, but the additional work per remote is short-string matching and does not multiply existing network calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded local comparisons without moving or multiplying network/filesystem work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve and start a remote MCP connection whose URL contains interactive variables
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing variable replacement resolves the URI before policy evaluation and creation of the remote HTTP/SSE connection. This PR enables the stored URL template to contain input references; it does not add another connection or an additional resolution pass on each protocol message.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open and use the remote MCP HTTP/SSE connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One connection per explicitly started remote server, with lifecycle and parallelism unchanged by this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Remote MCP servers already opened the same connection after configuration resolution. The diff changes how a registry URL template is generated, not connection count or scheduling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The connection is the dominant startup boundary; URL input resolution and policy checking must complete first.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of remote servers explicitly started and number of placeholders in each URL; no per-message or per-tool-call replacement was introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Connection concurrency remains driven by existing server start requests. No Promise.all, queue, limiter, or backpressure behavior is changed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Input persistence and runtime connection caching/lifecycle remain unchanged. Fixed values generate no prompt; interactive values use the existing variable resolver.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the diff changes configuration generation only and does not alter runtime boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote endpoint latency varies independently of this change; the new local preprocessing is negligible relative to the existing network startup boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Existing network startup cost and concurrency are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 10 changed files and every diff hunk for performance. Traced gallery pagination, registry synchronization, policy checks, install-time conversion/persistence, and remote connection startup. The PR adds bounded string/regex work and small temporary collections but no hot-loop UI work, retained lifecycle state, cache regression, extra boundary call, or concurrency burst. No findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
